notes: §1985:VIII.4.3.2 prints DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ] [ END-DELETE ], RECORD and KEY being optional words. deleteStatement parses it and BindDelete binds it for a relative file (a record-name or undefined name is COBOL1639), and what the later editions add is refused at 85: RETRY by VisitRetryPhrase and DELETE FILE by VisitDeleteFileStatement (each COBOL0900); an AT END, ON EXCEPTION or ON SIZE ERROR phrase and a second INVALID KEY phrase are syntax errors through Associates, which lets DELETE own the INVALID KEY pair only. Probed at --std 85: the format with and without RECORD, KEY, either phrase and END-DELETE compiles and runs. What is not implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates ask only that a phrase is printed by the format and not yet written, with no edition arm for the order, so NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY compiles and runs at 85; either order is the 2002 change (§2002:F.2 item 33). The same mechanism was recorded for the indexed DELETE, READ, REWRITE, START and WRITE formats. The witness deletes a record and then fails to delete it again, both in the printed order with END-DELETE.

next.reason: 1985: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2 ]"; 2023: "DELETE file-name-1 RECORD [ retry-phrase ] ┌ │ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 │ ┐ … NOT INVALID KEY imperative-statement-2". 2023 Format 1 adds an optional retry-phrase. Its choice indicators also let INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY appear in either order, where 1985 fixed the order, so more programs are accepted.
